title: Machine-guided microscopy characterizes an atypical ataxia presentation
summary: Unsupervised image analysis detected cellular patterns not apparent by inspection in an investigation of one family with an atypical ataxia presentation. Additional cell experiments found altered ataxin-7 behavior and mitochondrial bioenergetic deficits. The proposed combined role of ATXN7 and TOP1MT variants remains a hypothesis: unaffected parents carried individual variants, and fly models did not reproduce the patient phenotype.
organization: McMaster University; University of British Columbia; University of Toronto; University of Pittsburgh

evidence.tested: Patient-derived cells, functional measurements and fly models were examined.
evidence.unknown: Clinical causality, variant interaction and diagnostic utility are not established by this small study.
evidence.ai_role: PhenoRipper unsupervised image-pattern analysis supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract, selected image-analysis Methods, Results, Discussion, dates and affiliations; supplement not reviewed.
